 The Cyclones are back home Saturday morning to take on the Cincinnati Bearcats at 11:00 a.m. at Jack Trice Stadium. Iowa State is coming off a road loss to the Baylor Bears in a game in which they stormed out to a 10-0 lead. Jimmy Rogers and the Cyclones will look to take another step toward bowl eligibility with a win over the Bearcats on Saturday. See what the Cyclone Fanatic staff has to say about the Cyclones and the Bearcats. 
 Chris Williams (8-1) 
 Iowa State should be able to run the ball consistently against this team. Of course, I have major concerns about the defense at this point in the season. But with a home crowd behind them, I expect the Cyclones to get it done.  Iowa State 34, Cincinnati 30 
 Jake Brend (7-2) 
 Iowa State returns to Jack Trice Stadium, a place they’ve been pretty good this year. Slowing down Cincy’s rushing attack will be a big challenge for the Cyclone defense, especially one that has struggled with tackling. However, Cincy has some defensive problems as well. Can they account for Aiden Flora? I don’t think so. Flora runs wild, the Cyclones win a shootout. Iowa State 41, Cincinnati 34 
 Rob Gray (7-2) 
 The Bearcats’ rushing attack is among the nation’s best and quarterback JC French IV has been efficient as a passer with 15 touchdowns and three interceptions. The Cyclones, meanwhile, have fielded one of the worst scoring defenses in Big 12 play but showed signs of life in last week’s loss at Baylor despite surrendering 42 points. ISU’s offense does just enough to get the win. Cyclone running back Aiden Flora should have a big day and quarterback Jaylen Raynor will continue his late-season surge. Iowa State 34, Cincinnati 27 
 Jackson Pence (6-3) 
 Crazy to think the Cyclones only have three regular-season games left. I really hope this team can find a way to win two more and get to bowl eligibility because, despite everything they’ve dealt with, they’ve been a fun group to watch.
 This probably isn’t going to be one of those seasons we look back on like 2017, 2020 or 2024, filled with huge upsets and unforgettable moments. But it could be remembered as the start of something. This has been the beginning of the building process Jimmy Rogers started when he took over the job just 11 months ago, and I think we’ve already seen plenty of reasons to be excited about where it’s headed.
 Cincinnati is better this year, and with the rushing attack it has, this is still a team capable of jumping up and beating anybody. The Cyclones have to find a way to get stops despite all the injuries they’re dealing with defensively. On the other side, Jaylen Raynor and this Iowa State offense continues to get better each week, and I think we see another big performance Saturday.
 Give me the Cyclones in another high-scoring affair. Iowa State 41, Cincinnati 38 
 Jacqueline Cordova (6-3) 
 The end of Q3 is looming in corporate America, so I haven’t had much time to develop strong feelings about Saturday this week. All I know is the Cyclones aren’t losing, and I’m simply not entertaining any other outcome. Iowa State 38, Cincinnati 27 
 Derek Duke (8-1) 
 My main concern for Iowa State is stopping the run. Cincinnati has the second-best rushing offense in the Big 12, and Iowa State is in the bottom four of the conference when it comes to run defense. However, the Bearcats aren’t exactly great at stopping the run either as they sit below Iowa State giving up 169.3 per game on the ground.
 Injuries are still piling up for the Cyclones but with this game being at home, I feel a little more confident as the Bearcats have not won a road game this season. Plus, I feel like Iowa State’s offense has looked much better the last two weeks. Iowa State 31, Cincinnati 28
